reading.body:
The directory counts 450 AI tools across 23 categories, but only 63 have in-depth profiles covering pricing, strengths, weaknesses, and governance notes.

The gap between 450 listed tools and 63 profiled ones is the real finding. A catalog entry tells you a product exists. A profile tells you what it costs, where it fails, and what rules apply to it. Most of this market is visible only at the level of existence.

That matters for AI specifically because tool selection is where compute and power constraints reach the buyer. A team choosing a product is choosing how much inference it will run, and therefore how much electricity and capacity it will need. Pricing and weakness data are the inputs to that decision. Governance notes are the inputs to whether the decision survives review.

What the data does not cover is everything else. There is no list of the 450 tools, no breakdown of the 23 categories, and no indication of which of the 63 profiles are commercial versus open source. The counts are stated, not shown. The refresh interval is seven days, so the numbers move, but nothing here says how fast the underlying market moves.
